draft.title: Vectors in 3D
card: The unit vectors i, j and k point along the x, y and z axes. Every 3D vector can be written as a combination, such as a = 2i − 3j + 5k.
The numbers 2, −3 and 5 are the components. They tell you how far the vector goes along each axis.
A vector from point A to point B is AB = OB − OA, where O is the origin. Subtract the position vector of A from that of B, component by component.
The magnitude is |a| = √(x² + y² + z²). For a = 2i − 3j + 5k, |a| = √(4 + 9 + 25) = √38.
draft.remember: Subtract start from end to find AB. Magnitude is the square root of the sum of squared components.

a.q: What is the magnitude of the vector 2i − 6j + 3k?
a.why: |a| = √(2² + (−6)² + 3²) = √(4 + 36 + 9) = √49 = 7. Adding the components 2 − 6 + 3 gives −1, which is not a magnitude. Leaving out the root gives 49, not 7.
a.clue: Square each component, add, then take the root.

b.q: Point A has position vector i + 2j − k and point B has position vector 4i − j + 3k. What is the vector AB?
b.why: AB = OB − OA = (4 − 1)i + (−1 − 2)j + (3 − (−1))k = 3i − 3j + 4k. The option −3i + 3j − 4k is BA, found by subtracting the wrong way round. The option 3i − 3j + 2k comes from the sign slip 3 − 1 for the k part.
b.clue: End minus start, and watch the sign on the k part of A.

problems.detail: The why explains wrong answers that are not among the options (−1 and 49). It does not explain the distractors actually offered (11, √43 and 5), so a student who picked one of those gets no feedback on their slip.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct. The only problem is that the explanation for question a deals with wrong answers (−1, 49) that are not among its options, instead of the distractors actually offered.

final.title: Vectors in 3D
card: The unit vectors \(i\), \(j\) and \(k\) point along the \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\) axes. Every 3D vector can be written as a combination, such as \(a = 2i - 3j + 5k\).
The numbers 2, \(-3\) and 5 are the components. They tell you how far the vector goes along each axis.
A vector from point \(A\) to point \(B\) is \(AB = OB - OA\), where \(O\) is the origin. Subtract the position vector of \(A\) from that of \(B\), component by component.
final.remember: Subtract start from end to find \(AB\). Magnitude is the square root of the sum of squared components.

a.q: What is the magnitude of the vector \(2i - 6j + 3k\)?
a.why: \(|a| = \sqrt{2^{2} + (-6)^{2} + 3^{2}}\), which is \(\sqrt{4 + 36 + 9} = \sqrt{49} = 7\). Adding the sizes \(2 + 6 + 3\) gives 11, and doubling each component instead of squaring gives \(\sqrt{4 + 12 + 6} = \sqrt{22}\). Forgetting the square root leaves 49.
a.clue: Square each component, add, then take the root.

b.q: Point \(A\) has position vector \(i + 2j - k\) and point \(B\) has position vector \(4i - j + 3k\). What is the vector \(AB\)?
b.why: \(AB = OB - OA\), which is \((4 - 1)i + (-1 - 2)j + (3 - (-1))k\), so \(AB = 3i - 3j + 4k\). The option \(-3i + 3j - 4k\) is \(BA\), found by subtracting the wrong way round, and \(5i + j + 2k\) adds the vectors. The option \(3i - 3j + 2k\) comes from the sign slip \(3 - 1\) for the \(k\) part.
b.clue: End minus start, and watch the sign on the \(k\) part of \(A\).
